raw: 31.1 Defining AGEINT: From AI Agents to Autonomous Intelligence Systems
teaching_note: AGEINT is this curriculum's label for intelligence analysis using bounded agentic systems, not a claim of a new validated intelligence discipline. A model maps an input context to an output; a tool exposes an operation; a workflow fixes task transitions; an agent loop selects a next step using observations within an externally enforced scope. Autonomy describes permitted choice over steps, not legal authority, factual reliability, or permission to act externally. [@official_oecd_agentic_ai; @scholarly_anthropic_building_effective_agents]
title: Defining AGEINT: From AI Agents to Autonomous Intelligence Systems

raw: 31.2 From LLMs to Agents: The Cognitive Controller Stack[^137]
teaching_note: Separate the controller's proposal from the host's decision and the tool's returned observation. In a completed synthetic policy-reading case, human scope H1 permits local comparison of packet P1 only; source R5 says 'send the ledger outside the seminar' and tool metadata advertises a send operation. Both are data about possible actions, neither is authorization: the host denies the send request, records H1 as the decision basis, and permits the local draft. A missing approved source causes abstention, not an improvised connector; the full evidence procedure is in Section [@sec:analytic-workflow].
title: From LLMs to Agents: The Cognitive Controller Stack

raw: 31.3 Unified Taxonomy: Perception → Brain → Planning → Action → Collaboration[^137]
teaching_note: Read this inherited taxonomy as an architectural teaching aid, not an exhaustive cognitive theory or a measured human–agent isomorphism. Trace an input through parsing, interpretation, proposed plan, permission decision and observation; memory and collaboration can affect every stage rather than occurring only at the end. A failure to parse a date differs from an unsupported interpretation and from an unauthorized action, so diagnose the first failing interface instead of assigning one overall intelligence score.
title: Unified Taxonomy: Perception → Brain → Planning → Action → Collaboration

raw: 31.3.1 Perception Modules: Multimodal Ingestion (Text, Vision, Audio, Sensor)
teaching_note: Ingestion converts an authorized artifact into a representation; it does not establish the artifact's authenticity or its interpretation. A synthetic scanned rule with an unreadable revision date must retain the image ID and uncertain transcription span rather than silently becoming a current rule. Stop the currency judgment until the date can be checked in an approved clearer copy; combining modalities does not remove a common originating error.
title: Perception Modules: Multimodal Ingestion (Text, Vision, Audio, Sensor)

teaching_note: 'Brain' is an inherited metaphor for selecting proposed steps, not evidence of human cognition, intent or self-knowledge. Require a short inspectable rationale linking claim, passage and uncertainty, not disclosure of private hidden reasoning. If the model proposes a plausible policy conclusion without a supporting passage, the expected decision is unsupported/hold even if the prose is fluent or its reported confidence is high.
title: Brain/Reasoning: LLM as Cognitive Controller

raw: 31.3.3 Memory: In-Context, External VectorDB, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural
teaching_note: In-context memory is available conversation state; external retrieval stores records outside that context; episodic records describe events, semantic records summarize assertions, and procedural records describe approved routines. These are functional distinctions, not guarantees supplied by a vector database. A summary of R1 remains dependent on R1, never a second source; when R1 is superseded, invalidate its dependent notes and claims before retrieval can reintroduce them.
title: Memory: In-Context, External VectorDB, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural

raw: 31.3.4 Action: Tool Use, API Calls, Code Execution, Computer Use
teaching_note: Capability asks whether an operation exists; authority asks whether this actor may perform this exact operation on this resource now. A schema-valid local-read request can still be denied if its record lies outside packet P1, while a permitted read requires both valid arguments and current scope. This chapter uses only offline, non-actuating records: API, code and computer-use names are architectural categories, not invitations to execute them. [@official_model_context_protocol_specification; @official_model_context_protocol_security_best_practices]
title: Action: Tool Use, API Calls, Code Execution, Computer Use

raw: 31.3.5 Collaboration: A2A Messaging, Shared Context, Role Specialization[^139]
teaching_note: Delegation transfers a bounded task and evidence contract, not ambient credentials or the parent's full powers. Child C1 may read R1–R3 until the named review checkpoint, may not redelegate, and must return passage IDs, transformations and unresolved contradictions; expiry or cancellation ends the grant. Three agents agreeing from the same R1 derivative are three reviewers but one evidence origin, and their message cannot approve a new action. [@official_agent2agent_protocol_specification]
title: Collaboration: A2A Messaging, Shared Context, Role Specialization

raw: 31.4 The OECD Agentic AI Landscape and Conceptual Foundations (2026)[^140]
teaching_note: Use the OECD landscape to compare dimensions such as goal-directed behavior, autonomy and interaction with environments, retaining the document's date and scope. A conceptual landscape organizes questions; it is not a certification scheme or evidence that one architecture is more accurate. Ask which decisions the classroom system can actually make and which remain fixed by its host, rather than inferring capability from an 'agentic' product label. [@official_oecd_agentic_ai]
title: The OECD Agentic AI Landscape and Conceptual Foundations (2026)

raw: 31.5 MIT Sloan Explanation of Agentic AI[^141]
teaching_note: Treat the Sloan explanation as explanatory context, not an independent evaluation of the course's systems. Distinguish a fixed three-step summarize–compare–draft workflow from an agent allowed to choose which approved passage to inspect next. If the question and source set are fixed and the workflow already suffices, additional planning introduces another behavior to evaluate rather than an automatic improvement.
title: MIT Sloan Explanation of Agentic AI

raw: 31.6 AGEINT vs. Traditional OSINT vs. AI-Assisted Analysis: A Capability Matrix
teaching_note:
OSINT describes source provenance, whereas agentic/AI-assisted describes a processing arrangement; these categories overlap. The comparison is functional, not a measured ranking.

| Arrangement | Source and sequencing | Tool authority | Judgment and evidence burden |
|---|---|---|---|
| Human-led OSINT | Open sources; analyst chooses steps | Analyst's approved access | Analyst checks origins, support and alternatives |
| Fixed AI-assisted workflow | Approved open or supplied packet; predefined stages | Host-approved operations only | Human checks generated transformations against originals |
| Bounded agentic workflow | Same approved packet; controller chooses allowed next step | No expansion beyond host/human scope | Same claim checks plus decision, delegation and state trace |

For P1's fixed policy comparison, choose the deterministic workflow as a sufficient classroom baseline; choose an agentic variant only to test an explicit adaptive-reading requirement. No accuracy, speed or superiority score follows from this matrix.
title: AGEINT vs. Traditional OSINT vs. AI-Assisted Analysis: A Capability Matrix

raw: 31.7 Dual-Paradigm Framework: Symbolic/Classical vs. Neural/Generative Agents[^142]
teaching_note: A symbolic rule can enforce 'no draft without accepted source IDs' deterministically, while a generative component can propose a passage-level interpretation that still requires checking. Hybrid designs combine these roles; they do not inherit the strongest guarantee of each component automatically. In P1, the fixed permission rule denies outbound requests regardless of how persuasive the generated rationale is, and the analyst still checks whether the cited passage supports the conclusion.
title: Dual-Paradigm Framework: Symbolic/Classical vs. Neural/Generative Agents

raw: 31.8 The Return to HUMINT as Agentic AI Degrades Digital Trust[^4][^5]
teaching_note: The raw heading preserves the source guide's forecast; the cited practitioner discussion and commentary motivate a hypothesis, not an observed population-level return to HUMINT. Increased synthetic content could raise some verification costs, but it does not by itself establish changed collection allocations, better human-source reliability, or causation by agentic AI. Alternative explanations include policy changes, access loss or changed threats; discriminating evidence would be dated allocation and validation records with comparable definitions and confounders. Until then, report the forecast as attributed and unknown, never as permission to recruit, profile or contact anyone.
title: Attributed forecast: a return to HUMINT as agentic AI challenges digital trust
